sections.h2: Who bills you and who sets your value
sections.html:
Two offices at 33 Washington Street split the work. The Tax Collector sends the bill and takes payment, and the Tax Assessor sets the value the bill is built on. The counter is open weekdays from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. A dispute over value does not stay in the building: it goes to the Ocean County Board of Taxation, which supervises the assessor.

Toms River has been a calendar year town since January 2010, so the tax year matches the calendar and bills go out in July. If you are listing a house, expect the closing figures to rest on the current calendar year, divided into four installments.

Toms River is a shore township and the seat of Ocean County. The 2020 census counted 95,438 people, and a 2025 federal estimate puts the figure at 100,899. One assessor covers everything from mainland neighborhoods to the Dover Beaches communities on the Barnegat Peninsula, the barrier strip between Barnegat Bay and the Atlantic. Assessments can differ a lot from one part of town to another, so compare your value with what neighboring houses actually sold for.

Even owners with no loan carry about $917 a month in housing costs, which includes taxes and insurance.

Toms River collects in four installments, each followed by a ten day grace period. If the tenth day falls on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday, the grace period runs to the next business day.

  • Installment one, due February 1, covers January through March.
  • Installment two, due May 1, covers April through June.
  • Installment three, due August 1, covers July through September.
  • Installment four, due November 1, covers October through December.

Checks for current quarters go to a lockbox in Boston with the stub from your bill. Write your block and lot number on the check and enclose no letter. Payments from a bank bill-pay service go to P.O. Box 607 in Toms River, and the township warns they need extra days to arrive inside the grace period. An after-hours drop box at Town Hall takes tax payments only, and those post the next business day.

Appeals go to the Ocean County Board of Taxation, and the filing window closes April 1. A township-wide revaluation or reassessment moves that cutoff to May 1. For filing questions the assessor sends you to the board at 732-929-2008.

The assessor's FAQ makes two points. An appeal challenges your assessed value and has no effect on the tax bill itself, because the township, school district, county and fire districts set the budgets, not the assessor or the county board. And comparable assessments do not count as evidence of market value; only comparable sales do. Gather closed sale prices for similar Toms River houses before you file.

If you built or added something and received an Added Assessment bill, the appeal deadline is December 1 of the year the added assessment was placed. The date of the Certificate of Occupancy does not set the assessment date, because a home is valued when it is substantially ready for its intended use.

Qualified recipients receive a $250 deduction from the annual tax bill. Eligible groups are disabled persons, senior citizens, surviving spouses, veteran homeowners and the widows of veteran owners. Applications go through the Tax Assessor at 732-341-1000, extension 8300.

Two state programs also exist, the Property Tax Reimbursement Program and the Homestead Rebate Program. Ask the state Division of Taxation about eligibility and payment status. If you claim a deduction now, mention it to your attorney so the closing figures reflect it.

When taxes go unpaid, the township can sell a tax lien, which the owner or a mortgage holder can later redeem. Only a party with legal interest, meaning the owner, the owner's attorney or the mortgage holder, may redeem, and the request must be in writing. Verbal requests are refused.

  • Include the block and lot number and the lien certificate number.
  • State the date the payment will reach the Tax Collector, within 30 days of the request.
  • Add a daytime phone number, then fax the request to 732-505-1886 or mail it to P.O. Box 607. Email requests are not accepted.

The redemption statement takes time to prepare, so ask early in the sale. When a lien shows as paid but still appears in county records, request a certificate of redemption in writing, with a $25 check for each certificate, so the county clerk can clear it. A title company will run its own search, but you can check open liens first on the township's tax inquiry page. The payoff comes out of your sale proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: Handling the tax bill at closing
sections.html:
No new bill is issued when ownership changes, so hand the existing bill to the new owner at closing. A buyer left without one can ask the Tax Collector for a copy or print it from the township's online account lookup.

If a lender escrows your taxes and the loan ends at closing, the township wants written notice so the bank comes off its records. The notice needs the block and lot number, your mailing address, the bank's name and address, and the owner's signature. Skipping this step can leave a buyer with a duplicate bill and confusion over who paid the next quarter.

sections.h2: A seller's checklist for Toms River
sections.html:
Start with the Tax Collector: ask which installments are paid, whether any lien exists, and what the payoff looks like through your closing date. Next, confirm whether any deduction is on the account, since the Tax Assessor handles those applications. If a bank escrows your taxes, send the written notice with block and lot, your address and the bank's details, signed by the owner.

On closing day, give the buyer the current bill. Because Toms River collects by quarter, the closing agent normally divides the open installment between you and the buyer. A cash buyer purchasing as is skips the appraisal and loan approval wait, but the same tax steps apply, so none of this paperwork can be skipped.

faqs.q: Which phone number reaches the Toms River tax office?
faqs.a: Dial 732-341-1000 and ask for extension 8342 to reach the collector. Lines are staffed on weekdays and get busy near due dates, so leave a message. Value questions use extension 8300.

faqs.q: Does Toms River allow extra days after a due date?
faqs.a: Yes, ten days. A Saturday, Sunday or holiday on day ten pushes the deadline one business day later. Bank bill-pay checks can take several days to arrive, so send them early.

faqs.q: By what date must a Toms River owner file an assessment appeal?
faqs.a: April 1, moving to May 1 in a year with a township revaluation or reassessment. The county board takes the filing. Appeals of an Added Assessment close December 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Toms River house that has a tax lien on it?
faqs.a: Yes. The payoff comes out of proceeds, and a written redemption statement from the Tax Collector sets the figure. Only the owner, the owner's attorney or the mortgage holder may ask for it, and it takes time to prepare.

faqs.q: Does the new owner get a new tax bill after the sale?
faqs.a: No. The township mails no replacement when ownership changes, so the seller hands the existing bill to the buyer. The buyer can print a duplicate through the township's online tax account inquiry.
